title: Puffy Looks for the Rainbow
blurb: The rain stops, but no rainbow appears. Puffy the cloud and Flutter the butterfly set off on a colour hunt in the meadow.

pages.text: Pit, pat, pit… The rain stopped. Puffy the cloud stretched. “Now the rainbow will come out!” he said. Flutter the butterfly flapped her wings: “Hooray!”

piti.say: Now the rainbow will come out!

pages.ask: What do you see outside when the rain stops? What do you hear?

pages.text: Puffy looked right, looked left. No rainbow! No sun either. Puffy felt sad, his eyes filled with tears. “Where did the colours go?” Flutter came. “Let's play colour hunt while we wait for the sun!”
pages.ask: Why was Puffy sad? Who comes to you when you're sad?

pages.text: The colour hunt began! Flutter asked: “The first colour is red. Where is red hiding?” Puffy thought and thought. Hmmm…

predict.q: Where do you think they'll find red?
predict.res: Come on, let's look in the meadow together!

pages.ask: Where do you think red might be hiding? What red things can you see around you?

pages.text: Rustle rustle! Puffy bent down and looked. “Red!” Three reds were hiding in the meadow. A flower, a bug, a leaf.

mech.done: Red is done! Now for the other colours.

pages.ask: Which red do you think was hiding best? Why?

pages.text: Where's yellow? Where's blue? The flowers fell asleep in the rain. Snore, snore! Puffy whispered: “Good morning, yellow! Good morning, blue!”

mech.done: Yellow, orange, blue, purple! They're all awake.

piti.say: Good morning, yellow! Good morning, blue!

pages.ask: What did the meadow look like when the flowers opened? What's the first thing you do when you wake up in the morning?

pages.text: Flutter counted: “Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, purple… They're all here!” Just then, the sun woke up. Shine, shine! There's the rainbow! Puffy jumped: “I love blue the most!”

pirpir.say: Red, yellow, blue… They're all here!

pages.ask: What's your favourite colour? How does that colour make you feel?

kazanim: SNAB.2 Examining a work of art: The child examines the rainbow, the colours in the meadow and an ebru or picture shown in class; expresses feelings and thoughts with the question “Which did you like best, and why?” (SNAB.2.g).
TAOB.2 Making meaning from visual materials: Predicts from the pictures where red is hiding, connects what they see with the colours in their own surroundings.
TADB.2 Building new meaning from the story they hear: Makes inferences about why Puffy was sad and why he was happy in the end.
SDB1.1 Self-Knowledge and D7 Aesthetics: Says their own favourite colour, notices and names the things they find beautiful.
once: Point to Puffy on the cover: “What might this cloud be looking for?”
Look out of the window: “Which colours can we see outside right now?”
Say that in the story the sun brings the rainbow, and the colour hunt is a game played while waiting for the sun.
sirasi: On page 2, point to Puffy's face: “How is he feeling? Why?”
On page 3, accept both answers to the prediction question; then look together.
On page 4, say the name of the colour all together while finding the reds; on page 5, say each flower's colour as you touch it.
On the last page, point to the colours of the rainbow with your finger and name them in order.
sonra: Why was Puffy sad? Why wasn't the rainbow coming out? Who helped him?
Which colours did they find? Which one did you think was beautiful, and why?
When can we see a real rainbow? (When the sun comes out after rain; in the story, too, the rainbow came out when the sun woke up.)
Put the story in order with three pictures: Puffy sad, the reds found, the rainbow out.

sinif.materyal: Paper strips in red, yellow, blue, green, orange and purple; safe objects from the classroom; large paper and pastel crayons; an ebru paper or a colourful picture (printed or on a screen)
adim: Show an ebru paper or a rainbow-coloured picture: “Which colours can you see in this picture? How did it make you feel?” Accept every answer.
Give each child a colour strip. Say “Let's go on a colour hunt like Flutter!”; the children find an object of that colour in the classroom and bring it back.
Arrange the objects on the floor by colour in an arc like a rainbow, and say the name of each colour together.
Look at the “rainbow artwork” you have arranged: “Which part did you like best? How did it make you feel?” Each child says their favourite colour and adds a line to the big paper.

evSoru: How did Puffy feel when he found the rainbow?
Where did they find the reds?
What's your favourite colour? What do we have in that colour at home?

evEtk.d: Choose a colour and find three things in that colour at home or on a walk. When the sun comes out after rain, look up at the sky together; if you see a rainbow, name its colours.

guide.aileNotu: Today we read “Puffy Looks for the Rainbow”. Puffy the cloud and Flutter the butterfly played a colour hunt game in the meadow while waiting for the sun; when the sun woke up, the rainbow came out. A real rainbow forms when sunlight hits raindrops, too. At home, you can choose a colour together and find three things in that colour, and ask your child about their favourite colour and why.
